note: Asking prices in euros from the original listing on the day each home was added. Medians describe the homes RealHunt lists (cheap for their country, checked by a person), not a country's whole market. Rules, taxes and costs are general information, not legal or tax advice.
sentences: On 26 November 2026, RealHunt lists 3 homes for sale in the Czech Republic, each one checked by a person.
In the Czech Republic, the median asking price of those 3 homes is €159,600 (€1,464 per m², from the 3 homes with a known size); the cheapest costs €130,900 and the most expensive €179,700.
With 3 homes this is a small sample, so the median for the Czech Republic is a rough guide.

buying.costs_breakdown: There is no real estate transfer tax: it was abolished for purchases registered in the land register from December 2019. The land register (katastr nemovitostí) charges an administrative fee of CZK 2,000 for each application to register the sale (návrh na vklad); the notary or lawyer who draws up the contract is paid on top.
buying.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. Foreigners can buy homes and land in the Czech Republic on the same terms as Czechs: the limits on homes ended on 1 May 2009 and those on farmland and forest on 1 May 2011.
buying.annual_property_tax: Owners pay a yearly tax on land and buildings (daň z nemovitých věcí); from 2024 the rates rose to 1.8 times their old level on average, and each municipality can multiply the tax by a local coefficient between 0.5 and 5. The return is due by 31 January and the tax by 31 May.

homes.title: Maintained brick house with a heat pump and garden in Lomnička near Plesná, Cheb
homes.title_es: Casa de ladrillo mantenida con bomba de calor y jardín en Lomnička cerca de Plesná, Cheb
homes.summary: Asking 3,182,000 CZK (about €130,900). A maintained brick house in a quiet part of Lomnička, a village belonging to the town of Plesná in the Cheb district. About 120 m² of living space on a 378 m² plot: a large bright living room and a separate kitchen downstairs, a bedroom upstairs, a bathroom and a separate WC, plus a covered terrace, cellar, attic and a wooden shed in the garden. It is sold furnished and the advert says it can be lived in without major work. Heating is by a heat pump; mains water. The rooms are dated but clean.

homes.title: Renovated single-storey house with a 50 m² terrace and big garden in Častohostice
homes.title_es: Casa unifamiliar renovada con terraza de 50 m² y gran jardín en Částohostice
homes.summary: Asking 3,900,000 CZK (about €159,600), a private sale with no agency. A single-storey village house of 109 m² on a 1,078 m² plot in a quiet part of Častohostice, in the countryside of south-west Moravia. The photos show a fresh renovation: new laminate floors, white walls, exposed timber ceiling beams, a large open living and kitchen area and a new bathroom with a walk-in shower. The layout is four rooms plus kitchen, with a 50 m² terrace, a cellar and a garage. The advert says the house is in very good condition; it is sold unfurnished. Energy label D. The rear yard is still bare.

homes.title: Bright flat with two long balconies and a view over the old town of Litoměřice
homes.title_es: Piso luminoso con dos largos balcones y vistas sobre la ciudad antigua de Litoměřice
homes.summary: Asking 4,390,000 CZK (about €179,700). A 61 m² flat on the 6th floor of a block with two lifts in Litoměřice, a historic town on the Elbe, with views over the old centre and the hills of the České středohoří. The layout is two rooms plus a separate kitchen, and two balconies run along the whole width of the flat with access from every room. The bathroom, kitchen units and floors were renovated about 8 years ago; there are built-in wardrobes, a pantry and a cellar, with central heating. Shops, cafés and a bus stop are at the door and street parking is free. Building fees are not stated.
